description: A global day to honour workers and labourers — everyone who works hard to build society.
why_special: Workers — farmers, factory workers, teachers, doctors, drivers — are the backbone of the nation. This day recognises their contribution and fights for fair wages and conditions.

India's Labour Codes (2020) consolidate 29 laws into 4 codes to protect workers' rights.

description: India celebrates its freedom from British rule on 15 August 1947.
why_special: After nearly 200 years of British rule, India finally became independent. This was the result of a 70-year freedom struggle led by millions of Indians.
how_celebrated: The Prime Minister hoists the tricolour at the Red Fort in Delhi. The National Anthem "Jana Gana Mana" is sung. Kite flying is popular (especially in Gujarat and Rajasthan). Schools and offices hold flag-hoisting ceremonies. People wave small Indian flags and wear saffron, white, and green. India's national flag was designed by Pingali Venkayya. The flag has three colours: Saffron (courage), White (peace), Green (growth), and the Ashoka Chakra (24 spokes = progress). The National Anthem was written by Rabindranath Tagore and first sung in 1911. India's National Song "Vande Mataram" was written by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee. Pakistan also celebrates Independence Day on 14 August (one day earlier).
story: The British East India Company started ruling India in 1757 (Battle of Plassey). The Indian National Congress was formed in 1885. Mahatma Gandhi led movements: Non-Cooperation (1920), Salt March (1930), Quit India (1942). After WWII, Britain was weak and agreed to leave. On 15 August 1947, Lord Mountbatten (last Viceroy) transferred power. Jawaharlal Nehru became the first Prime Minister and gave the famous "Tryst with Destiny" speech. Lord Mountbatten said: "The sun has set on the British Empire, and the sun of a free India has risen."
